flagged.evidence: The definition sets “J_0=I” and then requires J J_i=-J_i J for “i<j.” For j=1 this includes i=0, so J=-J and J=0, contradicting J^2=-I. Thus P-hat_1 is empty and P_1 cannot be the component containing J_1; the index range needs to exclude 0.

The Statement identifies the midpoint component through J_1 in P_0 with P_1, but the cited definition makes P-hat_1 empty as written. For p=2 and J_1=[[0,-1],[1,0]], the minimizing geodesic gamma(t)=cos(pi t)I+sin(pi t)J_1 from I to -I has midpoint J_1, while no component P_1 containing J_1 exists.

The Statement assumes only a “compact band” with a finite union of critical manifolds, yet asserts that “Crossing one component” attaches its negative normal disk bundle. It supplies no regular sublevel endpoints or isolation of the critical value. For example, f(theta)=cos(2 theta) on S^1 has two nondegenerate critical points at the same maximum value, so a band crossing one cannot have the asserted regular complement.

After describing the local descending field, the proof says “Contracting v and stopping the outward u flow on the regular lower face gives the negative disk bundle attachment.” It does not construct the relative deformation or identify the resulting sublevel pair; the local flow formulas alone do not establish that global attachment.

Proof 3.1 applies [F2] to bypass each nonminimum handle, but [F2] depends on lem-relative-morse-bott-crossing-by-negative-normal-bundles, whose Statement lacks regular isolated crossing hypotheses and whose Proof 3.2 does not establish the relative attachment. Thus the claimed relative deformation into the minimum locus is not licensed by the cited dependency.
